solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Important PM meets the French and Germans at outset — EU going wrong way?

parts.note: John Major was the British Prime Minister in the 1990s
le is French for 'the'

indicators.note: at the outset means only the opening letter of each of these two words is taken
going the wrong way means the two letters of the abbreviation are read backwards

explanation.surface: A political headline asking whether a prime minister meeting French and German leaders sends Europe off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at outset' takes A and G from 'and Germans'; 'going wrong way' turns EU into UE.
explanation.definitionFit: Major-league is an American idiom from baseball's top division, used for anything big or significant.

clue.text: One saying little about university left hospital in French city

indicators.note: about means the quiet person's word goes around the other abbreviations

parts.note: a mouse is a timid quiet person who says little
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A taciturn academic leaves hospital in a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps MOUSE around U, L and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulhouse is an industrial city in Alsace in eastern France, near the Swiss and German borders.

clue.text: Unexpected jam — set up extra place to rest

indicators.note: unexpected suggests something turning out differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surprise traffic jam means setting up an extra seat to rest on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' looks like a reversal or a verb; it is part of the anagram fodder with 'jam'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump seat is a folding extra seat in a car, taxi or aircraft cockpit.

clue.text: It goes around — unchanged however you look at it

definitions.meaning: the spinning part of a machine

definitions.text: unchanged however you look at it
definitions.meaning: the word reads identically forwards and backwards, a palindrome, so it is the same from either direction

explanation.surface: Something revolving looks the same from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor spins in a helicopter or turbine, and its letters form a palindrome.

clue.text: Type of English, say? True — new version

indicators.note: a new version is a reworking, so the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a new version of a story is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say?' looks like 'for example'; it is fodder alongside 'True'. Estuary English is the accent of London and the Thames estuary area.
explanation.definitionFit: Estuary English is a British accent blending London and south-eastern speech, spread along the Thames estuary.

clue.text: Very unpleasant hag, sly, on the move, time to become involved!

indicators.note: on the move suggests the old woman's letters shifting position into a new order
to become involved means the letter for time is drawn into the middle of the cunning word

explanation.surface: A cunning old hag is on the move and it's time to get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' turns HAG into GHA; 'to become involved' puts T inside SLY, making STLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghastly means horrible or dreadful, a strong word for very unpleasant.

clue.text: Description of letter E that may startle?

definitions.meaning: E is the first letter of EYE, so it literally opens that word

explanation.surface: A description of the letter E turns out to be surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a revealing surprise; whimsically, E opens the word 'eye'.

clue.text: What might follow prayer mother initially thought

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Someone recalls what their mother thought should come after saying prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T from 'thought'. The definition is a fill-in: prayer is followed by this word in the phrase for a rug knelt on in worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer mat is the small rug Muslims kneel on, so the word follows 'prayer' in that compound.

clue.text: Swimmer's hairstyle

definitions.meaning: a fish, a swimmer; the 's stands for 'is'
a hairstyle short at front and sides and long at the back

explanation.surface: A swimmer's hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish and the short-front, long-back haircut share one name.

clue.text: Country bird

definitions.meaning: A country spanning Europe and Asia

explanation.surface: A rural bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation and the poultry bird share one name.

clue.text: Restrict books this person's plugging

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so the speaker's contraction goes into the middle of the word for books

parts.note: lit is short for literature, i.e. books
this person is the speaker, so 'this person is' becomes I'M

explanation.surface: A writer complains about limits on the books they are busy promoting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' looks like promotion, but it means filling a hole. 'this person's' is the setter speaking of themselves: 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to restrict it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: No stay-at-home type, one giving account about artist Vermeer at first

indicators.note: about means the storyteller's word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a teller is someone who tells a story, giving an account
RA is a Royal Academician, a standard abbreviation for an artist

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the painter's name is taken

explanation.surface: A storyteller recounts a journey taken by an artist interested in Vermeer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives V from Vermeer; 'about' says the storyteller goes around the artist and that V. RA (Royal Academician) is the standard artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is always on the move, the opposite of a homebody who never goes anywhere.

clue.text: Perceptive former pupil attending daily?

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day, a domestic servant

explanation.surface: An old pupil is asked whether they still go to school every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like 'every day', but in British usage a daily is a cleaning help, here a servant; 'attending' just puts OB next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An observant person notices things, which is what it means to be perceptive.

clue.text: Musical composition, calm, given a hearing

indicators.note: given a hearing means the word for calm is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds identical

parts.note: peace is calm or tranquillity

explanation.surface: A tranquil piece of music is played for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a hearing' says the synonym for calm is spoken: PEACE sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a single work of music, as in a piano piece.

clue.text: Chess champion's permit accepted by broadcaster

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: accepted by means the permit is taken into the middle of the broadcaster's name

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
a pass is a permit allowing entry

explanation.surface: A broadcaster agrees to give a chess champion a press pass.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Spassky was world chess champion from 1969 to 1972; Sky is the British satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Spassky, the Soviet grandmaster, held the world chess title before losing it to Bobby Fischer.

clue.text: Catholic wine in container — maybe funny in ironic way

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation and wine inside the container

parts.note: a sac is a pouch or bag-like container
RC is short for Roman Catholic
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Catholic wine is kept in a container, which some may find ironically amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy; 'in' puts the Catholic abbreviation and the wine into the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcastic remarks use irony to mock, and may be meant as humour.

clue.text: American's refusal recalled by king

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for refusal is read backwards

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a refusal
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An American's refusal is called back by a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NAY into YAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is informal British slang for any American, shortened from Yankee.

clue.text: Dance girl brought over musical group

indicators.note: in a down clue, being brought over means placed on top, ahead of the next part

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A girl brought a band over for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' suggests a reversal, but in a down clue it puts SARA above BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A saraband is a slow stately dance in triple time, popular in the Baroque era.

clue.text: Turncoat failing at core of work

parts.note: a defect is a failing or flaw

indicators.note: at the core of means only the central letters of the following word are taken

explanation.surface: A traitor's flaw lies at the heart of their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at core of' takes OR from the middle of 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: A defector abandons their side for another, which is what a turncoat does.

clue.text: Forward paid pittance originally

parts.note: a pro, or professional, is paid for playing

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A sports forward was originally paid a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a verb or adjective; it is a rugby position. 'originally' gives P from 'pittance'.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a prop is one of the forwards, the front-row players in the scrum.

clue.text: Paella freshly prepared served with English drink

indicators.note: freshly prepared suggests the dish is made anew, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh paella is served with an English beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly prepared' turns PAELLA into PALEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale ale is a light-coloured beer, a type of drink.

clue.text: Grass in this place appropriate to be included

indicators.note: to be included means the word for appropriate goes inside the word for this place

parts.note: here means in this place
to bag something is to appropriate or seize it

explanation.surface: Someone decides this is the right spot to include some grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective (suitable) but is the verb, to take: BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is herbaceous vegetation, especially grass used as pasture for grazing.

clue.text: Agent's name given by republican

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: An agent's name is supplied by a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: A handler manages or runs someone, like an agent controlling a spy or a performer.

clue.text: Relation from America in the money

indicators.note: in means the country's abbreviation goes inside the money

parts.note: coin is money in general
US is America

explanation.surface: A rich relative from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the money' reads as 'rich', but 'in' is the container signal and 'the money' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family relative, the child of an aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Deeply religious, extremely divine — very unfashionable?

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters, of the following word

parts.note: out means out of fashion, unfashionable

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being deeply religious is very out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes DE from 'divine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Devout people are earnestly pious, the meaning of deeply religious.

clue.text: Last of series, "Ring" — extremely impressive

parts.note: the letter O is round like a ring
mega is slang for extremely impressive

explanation.surface: A review of the final episode of a series about a ring calls it superb.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'Ring' suggest a title, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the last of a series.

clue.text: Portrait turned on its side for printers?

definitions.text: Portrait turned on its side for printers?

parts.words: Portrait turned on its side for printers?
parts.note: printers and word processors describe page orientation as portrait (tall) or its rotated alternative (wide), named after a type of painting

explanation.surface: A portrait painting is rotated by ninety degrees before being printed.
explanation.walkthrough: Portrait looks like a painting of a person; it is the upright page setting. Turned sideways it becomes the wide setting, which shares its name with a painting of scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Landscape orientation is the wide page layout, a portrait page rotated through a right angle.

clue.text: Gets a break, characters leaving weapon

indicators.note: characters leaving means some letters drop off each end, leaving the answer inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break and some characters leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove letters from the ends of 'Gets a break' and the answer sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a curved cavalry sword, a weapon also used in fencing.

clue.text: Arrange about hotel before some time in US — deficit results

indicators.note: before places the first part ahead of the season
about means the word for arrange goes around the letter for hotel

parts.note: to sort is to arrange
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
fall is the American word for autumn, a time of year

explanation.surface: Organising a hotel stay before an American autumn trip leaves someone out of pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts H inside the verb for arrange; 'before' sets that ahead of the American word for autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is an amount by which something falls short, the same as a deficit.

clue.text: Gust that's annoying

definitions.meaning: a sudden strong gust of wind
...! is an exclamation of annoyance, as in 'that's annoying'

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a sudden irritating gust of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast of air is a gust, and 'blast' as an interjection expresses irritation.

clue.text: Regularly used insect trap

indicators.note: regularly used means only every other letter of the following word is taken, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A device often used to catch insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly used' takes the even letters of 'insect'.
explanation.definitionFit: A net is a mesh used to catch fish, butterflies or insects, so it is a kind of trap.

clue.text: Somehow declare here's one providing encouragement

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
here supplies the letters; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone announces the arrival of a person who will cheer everyone on.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'here's' stands for 'is' and links to the definition; only HERE joins DECLARE in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerleader leads a crowd in supportive chants, literally or figuratively giving encouragement.
